title: Inside the Sewing Box
cardDescription: Familiar sewing tools, small supplies, and the parts that make them useful.
description: Open the sewing box for a crossword about familiar tools, small supplies, and the everyday words used at a sewing table.
focus: This puzzle looks at the contents of a sewing box and what each item does. Some clues name a whole tool, while others name one of its parts or a small supply. The definitions describe their purpose without requiring a sewing pattern.
solvingTip: Ask whether the clue describes something that cuts, carries thread, protects a finger, or holds supplies. A small part of a tool has its own name. Use short answers for those parts to help cross longer tool names.
words: Slender pointed sewing tool with a hole for thread
Fine strand passed through fabric to make stitches
Small finger cover that helps push a sewing needle
Small pointed fastener that holds fabric temporarily
Large scissors designed for cutting fabric
Two-bladed cutting tool with finger loops
Small spool supplying the lower thread in many sewing machines
Cylinder around which sewing thread is wound
Flexible measuring strip used by a dressmaker
Straight measuring tool marked with units
Temporary marking material used by a tailor
Seam ___: small tool that removes unwanted stitches
Hole at the blunt end of a hand-sewing needle
Sharp end of a sewing needle
Line where pieces of fabric are joined by stitches
Material cut and sewn to make clothing
One complete pass of thread through fabric
Small sewing supply, such as a button or snap
Small container that holds sewing tools
To make a short quick cut with scissors

answerNotes.THIMBLE: A thimble covers a fingertip used to push a needle. It is a protective pushing aid rather than a cutting tool.
answerNotes.SHEARS: Sewing shears are larger cutting tools intended for fabric. Scissors and shears can overlap in everyday speech, so the clue includes their size and purpose.
answerNotes.BOBBIN: In many sewing machines, the bobbin supplies the lower thread. A separate upper thread passes through the needle.
answerNotes.SPOOL: A spool holds wound thread. Bobbins are also small spools, but the machine-related clue gives bobbin a more specific role.
answerNotes.TAPE: Tape means a flexible measuring strip here. It does not refer to an adhesive strip used to stick things together.
answerNotes.EYE: Eye names the opening through which thread passes. The same word names a body part, but the needle setting identifies the tool part.
answerNotes.RIPPER: Seam ripper is the complete tool name. Ripper fills the blank; the tool removes stitches rather than cutting out a new fabric piece.
answerNotes.NOTION: Notion has a sewing meaning: a small supply or accessory. It does not mean an idea in this clue.

title: A Basket of Knitting
cardDescription: Yarn, simple knitting vocabulary, and familiar knitted items.
description: Settle beside a yarn basket with a crossword about knitting words, the material on the needles, and familiar things made from it.
focus: The clues combine knitting actions and textures with yarn terms and finished garments. Some familiar words take a craft meaning here. The clues give direct definitions, so reading knitting abbreviations or following a chart is not required.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue asks for a material, a tool, a fabric texture, or a finished item. A word for a yarn bundle differs from a word for a loop in the fabric. Use the garment clues to cross the more specialized knitting vocabulary.
words: To form fabric by working interlocking yarn loops with needles
Knitting stitch that shows a small bump on the side facing the worker
Long slender knitting tool that holds live stitches
Continuous strand worked into knitted fabric
A loosely coiled bundle of yarn
Rounded bundle of wound knitting yarn
A single loop forming part of knitted fabric
One horizontal line of knitting stitches
Raised vertical ridge in a stretchy knit-and-purl pattern
Twisted-looking knitting pattern made by crossing groups of stitches
Number of knitting stitches or rows over a measured distance
Person who makes fabric using yarn and needles
Long narrow knitted garment worn around the neck
Hand covering with one thumb section and a shared finger section
Knitted foot covering worn inside a shoe
Fiber from sheep commonly spun into knitting yarn
How tightly or loosely a worker holds the knitting yarn
Close-fitting knitted band at a sleeve's end
Curved length of yarn that forms a knitting stitch

answerNotes.PURL: A purl stitch shows a small bump on the side being worked. It is the reverse appearance of a knit stitch viewed from the other side.
answerNotes.SKEIN: Skein names a loosely coiled yarn bundle. Yarn can also be wound into balls or other forms, so the shape in the clue matters.
answerNotes.ROW: A row is a horizontal line of stitches. A single stitch is one unit within the fabric rather than the whole line.
answerNotes.RIB: Ribbing uses alternating knit and purl sections to make raised vertical ridges. The word rib here refers to the fabric texture.
answerNotes.CABLE: A knitted cable looks twisted because groups of stitches cross over one another. It is a fabric pattern rather than an electrical wire.
answerNotes.GAUGE: Knitting gauge counts stitches or rows within a measured distance. It is related to, but different from, how tightly someone holds the yarn.
answerNotes.MITTEN: A mitten groups the fingers together and has a separate thumb section. A glove gives each finger its own section.
answerNotes.TENSION: Tension describes how tightly or loosely the yarn is held. It can affect stitch size and therefore the measured gauge.
answerNotes.CUFF: A cuff is a band at a sleeve's end. In a knitted garment it may use a stretchy texture, but its position is what the clue identifies.

title: With a Crochet Hook
cardDescription: A crochet hook, linked loops, and familiar decorative projects.
description: Pick up a crochet-themed crossword about a hook and yarn, the shapes they form, and familiar handmade projects.
focus: This puzzle follows basic crochet tools, shapes, and project words. Clues describe an item's shape or purpose rather than using abbreviated stitch instructions. Some answers are ordinary words with a particular craft meaning.
solvingTip: Check whether the clue asks for a tool part, a shape, an action, or a finished piece. A line of linked loops and a circular course of stitches are different structures. Crossing letters can help with longer decorative words.
words: Tool with a curved tip used to pull yarn through crochet loops
Strand pulled through loops with a crochet hook
Series of linked loops often used to begin crochet
Ringlike bend of yarn caught by a crochet hook
Small decorative unit that can be repeated in a crochet project
Four-equal-sided shape used in a familiar granny-style crochet unit
To reverse the direction of work at the end of a crochet row
Loose yarn end left at the beginning or end of a project
Small clip or ring used to identify a crochet stitch
Decorative edging added around a crocheted piece
Loose hanging yarn strands used as decoration
Small decorative openwork mat for a table
Crocheted or knitted blanket often used as a throw
Part of a crochet hook held in the hand
End of a crochet hook that catches the yarn
Wrap worn over the shoulders, sometimes crocheted
Plant fiber often used for crocheted dishcloths
Delicate openwork fabric that can be made with a crochet hook

answerNotes.HOOK: A crochet hook catches yarn and draws it through loops. Knitting commonly uses two or more needles instead, although both crafts can use yarn.
answerNotes.CHAIN: A crochet chain is a series of linked loops. The word names a yarn structure here rather than a line of metal links.
answerNotes.MOTIF: A motif is a design unit that can repeat in a larger project. It may be a square or another shape; the word does not require one fixed outline.
answerNotes.ROUND: Round names a circular course of stitches here. It differs from a straight row worked back and forth.
answerNotes.TAIL: Tail means a loose end of yarn in this craft setting. It is not a part of an animal in the clue.
answerNotes.MARKER: A stitch marker identifies a location in the work. The word marker here refers to that small clip or ring rather than an ink pen.
answerNotes.FRINGE: Fringe consists of loose strands along an edge. It differs from a solid stitched border, even though both can decorate a project.
answerNotes.DOILY: A doily is a small decorative mat, often made with openwork. It is usually displayed on a surface rather than worn as clothing.
answerNotes.AFGHAN: Afghan has a textile meaning: a knitted or crocheted blanket. The clue asks for that household item.

title: A Patchwork Quilt for the Sofa
description: Piece together the familiar fabrics, tools, and cozy uses of a patchwork quilt.
cardDescription: Piece together the familiar fabrics, tools, and cozy uses of a patchwork quilt.
subtheme: A Patchwork Quilt for the Sofa
focus: Small fabric patches are joined into a larger cover. These clues use everyday sewing and household words.
solvingTip: Start with a tool, fabric, or place where the quilt is used.

Small piece of fabric in the quilt's design

answerNotes.QUILT: A quilt joins several layers rather than being one plain sheet.
answerNotes.PATCH: Patches can have different shapes and colors.
answerNotes.SEAM: A seam joins pieces, while an outer edge marks the boundary.
answerNotes.COTTON: Cotton is a material, not a particular quilt pattern.
answerNotes.NEEDLE: The thread passes through the needle's eye.

title: Mending Everyday Clothes
cardDescription: Small clothing repairs, worn areas, and everyday fasteners.
description: Give a favorite garment another turn through a crossword about small repairs, familiar fasteners, and places where clothing wears.
focus: This puzzle looks at everyday mending vocabulary. Some clues name a repair action, while others describe a damaged area, part of a garment, or a fastening. The definitions focus on familiar words rather than step-by-step repair instructions.
solvingTip: Look for whether the clue describes damage, a way to fix it, or a part that holds clothing closed. A fabric piece added over damage differs from the inner layer sewn inside a garment. Short edge and fastening clues can help with longer answers.
words: To fix a small damaged area of clothing
To repair a fabric hole by weaving thread across it
Separate piece of fabric sewn over a damaged area
Folded and stitched lower edge of a garment
Small disk sewn onto clothing to fasten it through a hole
Clothing fastener with two parts that press together
Fastener with interlocking teeth closed by a sliding pull
An open gap worn through a piece of clothing
A rip in clothing caused by pulled-apart fabric
To unravel into loose threads along a fabric edge
To join or repair fabric with a needle and thread
To restore a damaged garment to usable condition
Band at a shirt sleeve's wrist opening
Bent-arm area where a jacket may need a reinforcement patch
Leg-joint area where trousers often wear thin
Inner fabric layer sewn inside a coat or jacket
Small ring of thread or fabric that can hold a button
Curved metal clothing fastener paired with an eye
To secure a garment with a closure
To smooth fabric by applying an iron

answerNotes.DARN: Darning rebuilds a small damaged area with interwoven thread. A patch instead adds a separate piece of fabric over or around the damage.
answerNotes.PATCH: Patch is a noun here for a separate piece of repair fabric. It differs from the thread woven across a hole when darning.
answerNotes.HEM: A hem is the folded and stitched edge of a garment. It is an edge finish rather than a fastener used to hold an opening closed.
answerNotes.BUTTON: A button passes through a hole or loop to fasten clothing. A snap closes by pressing two matching parts together.
answerNotes.SNAP: Snap is the American name for this press-together clothing fastener. Press stud is another name commonly used in British English.
answerNotes.ZIPPER: A zipper closes with interlocking teeth and a moving slider. The clue describes the mechanism rather than a button or a snap.
answerNotes.TEAR: Tear means a rip in fabric here and rhymes with hair. The spelling is also used for a drop from the eye, pronounced differently.
answerNotes.FRAY: Fray describes an edge unraveling into loose threads. A clean cut or a single hole can be a different kind of damage.
answerNotes.HOOK: Hook refers to one half of a hook-and-eye closure here. A crochet hook shares the curved shape but serves a different purpose.
answerNotes.PRESS: Press means smooth with an iron in this clothing context. It does not mean push a button or squeeze two fastening parts together.
